newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African, U.S. funds in 60 mln rand share swap.
newsitem.headline: S.African, U.S. funds in 60 mln rand share swap.

text.p: A South African and a U.S. institution swapped 60 million rand of shares late on Tuesday, signalling tentative foreign institutional interest in South African assets, share dealers said on Wednesday.
The deal, which was done through London, saw the unnamed U.S. fund manager take South African shares from the local institution's portfolio in return for international equities.
Such swaps give South African funds exposure to overseas markets and foreign funds exposure to an emerging market.
South Africa's exchange control regulations were liberalised in June last year and local institutions are now allowed to swap up to 10 percent of their local assets for offshore investments.
But many foreigners have been reluctant to become involved, due to the volatility of the rand, and the international exposure of most South African funds remains well below the 10 percent limit.
Swap activity has also been limited by Reserve Bank restrictions on discounts which may be offered in any deal.
The central bank said last November that around 20 billion rand of asset swaps had been approved since the system was first launched in July 1995, of which two thirds have been completed.
